extracted.intended_audience: program evaluators, MER organizers, education researchers, and NSF program officers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and methods for assessing the MER Forum's individual- and departmental-level activities (reach, communications, workshops, and systemic effects) using site visits, participant-observation, and a tailored survey program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent to which MER reaches its target audience of research mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the extent to which MER reaches its target audience of research mathematicians (MER’s claim to systemic reform implies reaching those in the community who may not already be interested in educational issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare survey respondent composition to national faculty counts; estimate proportions of target population reached (e.g., <1% of mathematicians); interpret in light of MER's mission and tradeoffs between exclusivity and breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of the Forum's communication activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how well MER's various communication channels (word of mouth, newsletters, special mailings, posted announcements, workshops, CBMS volumes, personal invitations, articles) attract and inform participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure which avenues respondents report as how they found MER and which they find helpful; distinguish channels that recruit new members (word of mouth, special mailings) from those that serve existing members (newsletters). Use survey percentages and open-ended comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth and depth of MER's educational initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the range (breadth) of topics MER addresses (K-12, undergraduate, calculus reform, pedagogy) and the substantive depth of its initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine newsletter content, workshop topics, CBMS volumes and session presentations to judge topical focus and balance between elementary/secondary and post-secondary concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of MER's workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the value and effects of MER workshops to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect participant reports on perceived usefulness; observe workshop sessions for pedagogy modeling and engagement; measure follow-up activity and membership recruitment attributable to workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent to which MER meets the needs of mathematicians and math and K-12 educators
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how well MER's activities satisfy the professional needs of different participant groups (mathematicians, math-educators in education departments, K-12 teachers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subgroup-specific questionnaires, analyze responses by professional community, and note low subgroup sample sizes when drawing inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic effects of MER's activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether MER contributes to broader systemic change in mathematics education beyond individual participants (e.g., influence on departmental reward structures or broader community practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of diffusion, influence on others not directly involved, publications, and institutional change; interpret with caution given small absolute numbers reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant-observation of conferences and workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Use participant-observation at Joint Societies Meetings, workshops, advisory meetings, and banquets to gather qualitative data (observe sessions, model pedagogy, interview attendees informally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record attendance levels, quality of pedagogy, degree of audience engagement, examples of discussion, and informal interviews; include observation of special sessions and banquet interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visit checklist and responsive case study approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine a priori checklist items with a responsive approach during site visits; checklist included interviewing department chair, meeting with graduate students, talking with pro-/neutral-/anti-MER individuals, and attending at least one 'reformed' mathematics class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select case sites purposively to maximize learning (best-case scenarios) and ensure geographic and programmatic representation; adapt activities to site-specific themes to balance pre-ordinate and responsive methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case selection for site visits (purposeful sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select institutions where evaluators expect to find active educational agendas (best-case scenarios) while ensuring geographic and programmatic representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When random selection would limit learning, use purposive selection to maximize depth of insight; document selection rationale (regions chosen, program types) and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey population approach (survey entire population vs sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: When subgroup membership cannot be reliably identified, survey the entire population rather than attempt probabilistic sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveying all 730 past and current participants was chosen because lack of descriptive identifiers prevented stratified sampling; acknowledge tradeoffs such as inability to compute precise subgroup response rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of professional community subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize at least three professional subgroups for analysis: (1) mathematicians/mathematical scientists/statistics/computer science, (2) mathematics educators in education departments, (3) K-12 teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruments and analysis plans that consider these subgroups; where subgroup membership is unknown, provide multiple questionnaire forms and instruct respondents which to complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument design: multiple tailored questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop three clearly labeled questionnaire forms (one per professional community) to avoid complicated skipping patterns and to ask pertinent, group-appropriate questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content/language to each professional community; clearly label forms and instruct respondents to return only the appropriate form; accept partially completed surveys to increase returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing with stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot test instruments multiple times with stakeholders (co-directors, advisory committee, task force, workshop participants) to 'learn the language' of participants and refine items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct iterative pilots in relevant meetings (e.g., MER workshop, task force meeting, advisory committee meeting); incorporate feedback from domain experts and co-directors into revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior instruments and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform instrument development by reviewing existing surveys and relevant literature (e.g., 1992 MER survey, 'Faculty at Work' survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine elements from prior validated instruments and stakeholder feedback to enhance relevance and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey administration techniques to boost response rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ practical techniques such as mailing follow-up postcards, offering small incentives (e.g., $2 MER coupon), and advising expected completion time (20–25 minutes) to encourage returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh incentive design (coupon may favor supporters) and resource constraints; use reminders approximately two weeks after mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging partial completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage respondents who cannot complete the entire survey to at least return demographic and closed-ended items to enrich analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State this explicitly in the cover letter to increase usable data even when full completion is not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response rate measurement and subgroup response limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report usable questionnaire return rate (e.g., 230 usable questionnaires, 32% overall) and note inability to precisely compute subgroup response rates when questionnaires were sent based on incomplete affiliation data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide subgroup counts (e.g., 199 mathematicians, 20 education, 11 K-12), estimate subgroup response rates where possible, and discuss limitations on representativeness due to self-selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic representativeness and stability indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use demographic variables (gender, race/ethnicity, academic rank, age, highest degree, organizational affiliations, years at institution) to assess representativeness and participant stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare respondent demographics to national benchmarks; note over/under-representation (e.g., higher percentage of women among MER participants than national average, high proportion of tenured/full professors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of inclusiveness vs elitism
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate perceptions of MER's inclusiveness and whether being a 'small subset' creates an image of elitism among the broader mathematics community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open-ended survey comments and interview data to capture perceptions (e.g., 'Make it less elitist', 'Open up the meetings'); weigh against mission needs to attract research mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of communication channels' differential roles (recruit vs retain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate which communication modes recruit new members (word of mouth, special mailings) versus those that retain/inform existing members (newsletters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey items asking 'How did you find out about MER?' and 'Is the MER newsletter helpful?' and analyze which sections of the newsletter are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of CBMS volumes' reach and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure awareness, readership, and perceived usefulness of CBMS Issues in Mathematics Education volumes among participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages aware/read and perceived usefulness categories (not at all, a little, considerably, extremely); note low awareness among K-12 respondents and limited recruitment utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of special sessions at Joint Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate special sessions by attendance, room capacity, topic relevance, quality of pedagogy, and ability to provoke discussion and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe session fill rates, note sessions with standing-room-only attendance, identify sessions that modeled good pedagogy, and record instances where controversial talks produced lively debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop/session topic alignment with target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether session topics align with MER's intended audience (e.g., MER addresses K-12 issues while MAA focuses on post-secondary), and whether overlap with other organizations dilutes or complements MER's distinctiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare session topics across sponsor groups (MER vs MAA), and evaluate whether MER's more controversial topics are a distinguishing feature; consider implications for recruitment and mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple data sources for triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine survey data, participant-observation, informal interviews, advisory committee feedback, and CBMS publication analysis to triangulate findings about MER's effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how each data source contributes to themes; acknowledge when small subgroup sizes or self-selection limit claims.
